identity.name: Democratic Kampuchea (Khmer Rouge)
native_names: កម្ពុជាប្រជាធិបតេយ្យ (Kâmpŭchéa Prâchéathippadey)

land.text: the whole of Cambodia: the Khmer Republic fell to the Khmer Rouge when Phnom Penh was captured on 17 April 1975

predecessors.note: The Khmer Republic (1970-1975) is carried inside the kingdom-of-cambodia dossier (a rename in 1970); the DK page lists 'Predecessor: 1975: Khmer Republic; 1976: GRUNK'.

land.text: Cambodia, taken by the Vietnamese army and the KUFNS: 'On 7 January 1979, the PAVN entered Phnom Penh along with members of the KUFNS'

successors.note: The Khmer Rouge kept the jungle on the Thai border and a government-in-exile (infobox: 'Government-in-exile (1979-1993)'; the Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea from 22 June 1982); that holdout is carried by the contest events of the People's Republic of Kampuchea dossier, not here.

capitals.name: Phnom Penh
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Phnom Penh'; the city was emptied after the capture ('Phnom Penh, populated by 2.5 million people, was soon nearly empty').

correction.text: the whole of Cambodia from the capture of Phnom Penh on 17 April 1975; the 1976 shape unchanged, with the years extended back to 1975

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Khmer Rouge row begins in 1976 (the constitution of 5 January 1976) but the infobox gives 'Khmer Rouge capture of Phnom Penh: 17 April 1975' and calls the name 'the official name of the Cambodian state from 1975 to 1979'. The shape is the 1976 shape; only the years change.

184,307 km2 for 1976-1978 against the infobox's 181,035 km2 (no year given): ratio 1.02. The outline is the same as the Kingdom of Cambodia's 1956 and 1996 rows (184,307 km2), which is Cambodia's modern territory; the page gives no border description beyond the Vietnamese refusal to 'recognize the Brévié Line' and the 1975 island clashes (Phu Quoc, Tho Chu, Poulo Wai), none of which moves a drawn cell. Cliopatria ends the row in 1978; the state ends on 7 January 1979 (ledger).

ledger.note: 1975: the Khmer Rouge capture Phnom Penh (17 April) and empty the city. Infobox 'Khmer Rouge capture of Phnom Penh: 17 April 1975'; 'The Khmer Rouge demanded and then forced the people to leave the cities and live in the countryside.'

region.text: the whole of Cambodia: 'the official name of the Cambodian state from 1975 to 1979' (lead)

ledger.note: 1975: the Khmer Rouge hold the country from the fall of the capital (17 April). The page dates the capture of Phnom Penh, not the last Republic-held ground (the kingdom-of-cambodia dossier dates the last area, Preah Vihear, to 22 May).

region.text: the island of Phú Quốc (invaded 1 May 1975) and, off the grid, the Thổ Chu Islands (10 May 1975) and Koh Poulo Wai (Vietnamese from late May to August 1975); the circle is the researcher's reading around Phú Quốc

ledger.note: May 1975: the Khmer Rouge raid Vietnamese islands. 'On 1 May 1975, the KRA invaded the Vietnamese island of Phú Quốc'; on 10 May it captured 'the Thổ Chu Islands, where it executed 500 Vietnamese civilians'; Vietnam 'then struck back and invaded the Kampuchean island of Koh Poulo Wai'. The land was South Vietnam's until 30 April and the PRG's and Hanoi's after; the counterpart is the democratic-republic-of-vietnam dossier, which holds the South in 1975.

region.text: the island of Phú Quốc (invaded 1 May 1975) and, off the grid, the Thổ Chu Islands (10 May 1975) and Koh Poulo Wai (Vietnamese from late May to August 1975); the circle is the researcher's reading around Phú Quốc

ledger.note: August 1975: the island dispute ends. 'In August 1975, Vietnam returned the island of Koh Poulo Wai to Kampuchea' (DK page: 'the Vietnamese evacuated Poulo Wai in August'); the pages do not say when the Khmer Rouge left Phú Quốc and Thổ Chu.

1976: the constitution of Democratic Kampuchea is promulgated (5 January); the Khmer Rouge 'abolished the Royal Government of National Union of Kampuchea (GRUNK; established in 1970)'. The page does not date the adoption of the name; Sihanouk resigned as head of state in April 1976 (the page gives 2, 5 and 'mid-April').

region.text: the Cambodian-Vietnamese frontier: 'a military attack against the Vietnamese provinces of An Giang and Châu Đốc' (30 April 1977), KRA forces 'advanced about 10 km into Tay Ninh Province' (1977); PAVN divisions 'crossed the border along several axes' (16 December 1977). One cell either side of the 1976 frontier is the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1977: the border war begins. On 30 April 1977 Kampuchean forces launched 'a military attack against the Vietnamese provinces of' An Giang and Châu Đốc; in September KRA forces 'advanced about 10 km into Tay Ninh Province'. The contest starts with the first attack; the frontier band is the reading.

region.text: 'PAVN divisions crossed the border along several axes' on 16 December 1977 and 'marched through Svay Rieng Province and only stopped short of entering the provincial capital'

ledger.note: December 1977: Vietnam invades. On 16 December 1977 PAVN divisions 'crossed the border along several axes' and by late December 'marched through Svay Rieng Province and only stopped short of entering the provincial capital'. How much of the province was held is the reading.

region.text: 'PAVN divisions crossed the border along several axes' on 16 December 1977 and 'marched through Svay Rieng Province and only stopped short of entering the provincial capital'

ledger.note: January 1978: Hanoi withdraws. On 6 January 1978 PAVN divisions were 'only 38 km from Phnom Penh', but 'the Vietnamese Government decided to withdraw its forces from Kampuchea'. A June 1978 thrust that 'pushed the KRA forces back into the provincial cities of' Suong and Prey Veng, 'then withdrew', is on the same page and moves no drawn border.

region.text: the Cambodian-Vietnamese frontier: 'a military attack against the Vietnamese provinces of An Giang and Châu Đốc' (30 April 1977), KRA forces 'advanced about 10 km into Tay Ninh Province' (1977); PAVN divisions 'crossed the border along several axes' (16 December 1977). One cell either side of the 1976 frontier is the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 7 January 1979: the border war ends in the fall of the capital. 'On 25 December 1978, 150,000 Vietnamese troops invaded Democratic Kampuchea' (a first offensive 'towards the town of Kratié' began on 21 December); 'On 7 January 1979, the PAVN entered Phnom Penh along with members of the KUFNS.'

region.text: Cambodia, taken by the Vietnamese army and the KUFNS; 'The Khmer Rouge was forced to retreat into the jungle near the border with Thailand'

ledger.note: January 1979: the Khmer Rouge lose the country. The PRK was 'established in Phnom Penh' on 8 January 1979; the Khmer Rouge retreat to the Thai border, but the page gives no extent for the land they kept (the PRK dossier carries that strip as a contest).
7 January 1979: Democratic Kampuchea falls. Infobox 'Vietnamese capture of Phnom Penh: 7 January 1979'; 'Phnom Penh fell to the advancing Vietnamese on 7 January 1979.'

wars.name: Cambodian-Vietnamese War

the Cambodian-Vietnamese frontier: 'a military attack against the Vietnamese provinces of An Giang and Châu Đốc' (30 April 1977), KRA forces 'advanced about 10 km into Tay Ninh Province' (1977); PAVN divisions 'crossed the border along several axes' (16 December 1977). One cell either side of the 1976 frontier is the researcher's reading
'PAVN divisions crossed the border along several axes' on 16 December 1977 and 'marched through Svay Rieng Province and only stopped short of entering the provincial capital'

wars.outcome: Vietnam and the KUFNS overthrew Democratic Kampuchea: Phnom Penh fell on 7 January 1979 and the People's Republic of Kampuchea was set up on 8 January; the Khmer Rouge withdrew to the Thai border.
wars.note: The page's infobox dates the war '23 December 1978 - 26 September 1989' and lists 'Thailand (border clashes)' with Democratic Kampuchea. This entry starts with the May 1975 island clashes and the 1977 border war and ends with the fall of the state; the war after 1979 belongs to the PRK dossier. The infobox gives 21 December 1978 for the first Vietnamese offensive (the DK page 21 December, the body 22 December); the page counts 25 December as the full invasion.

wars.name: Khmer Rouge border attacks on Thailand
wars.outcome: No change of border: 'Khmer Rouge forces attacked villages in the border areas of Thailand near Aranyaprathet.'
wars.note: The pages give no dates for the clashes with Thailand or with Laos ('incidents along the Laos border'), so there is no zone.

certainty.note: The land frontiers are the French-era surveyed lines; the sea border and the islands are disputed ('The Vietnamese refused to recognize the Brévié Line'; Poulo Wai, Phú Quốc and Thổ Chu changed hands in 1975), and the Vietnamese frontier is soft in 1977-1978, when the fighting moved it by kilometres.

sources.title: Cambodian-Vietnamese War
sources.note: Dated steps of the border war 1975-1979: Phu Quoc and Tho Chu (1 and 10 May 1975), Poulo Wai (August 1975), An Giang and Tay Ninh 1977, the December 1977 incursion and January 1978 withdrawal, the invasion of 21/25 December 1978, 7 January 1979, the retreat to the Thai border.

notes: The Cliopatria row is named Khmer Rouge and runs 1976-1978; the state is Democratic Kampuchea (infobox 17 April 1975 to 7 January 1979), so a new 1975 keyframe extends the shape back and the dossier ends in 1979. Wikipedia title 'Khmer Rouge' is Cliopatria's; the pages opened are 'Democratic Kampuchea' and 'Cambodian-Vietnamese War' (page budget 1-2). The Khmer Rouge after 7 January 1979 (the Thai-border jungle, the Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea from 22 June 1982, and the Pailin loss of 1989 recorded in the PRK dossier) are not in this dossier's life: the people-s-republic-of-kampuchea dossier carries the strip as a contest with khmer-rouge (1979-01 to 1991-10) and the Pailin loss (1989-10); a rebel dossier for the CGDK / Khmer Rouge zones 1979-1999 would belong to the additions batch. The Khmer Rouge's own liberated zones before 17 April 1975 (the kingdom-of-cambodia dossier's 1972 contest) are not drawn here either. The rulers strip is omitted: the infobox lists Pol Pot, Khieu Samphan, Norodom Sihanouk (1975-1976), Penn Nouth, Nuon Chea unlabelled and the page does not say which was head of state and which prime minister. The 1975 island events (Phu Quoc, Tho Chu, Poulo Wai) are mostly off the land grid, so they resolve to few cells; the counterpart for 1975 is the democratic-republic-of-vietnam dossier (which holds the South after 30 April 1975), for 1977-1978 the socialist-republic-of-vietnam (from 2 July 1976). The Mayaguez incident (the DK page dates the US air strike on Kompong Som to 'late May' 1975) and the Ba Chuc massacre (April 1978) are on the pages but move no border and are not events. The Thai and Lao border incidents are undated on both pages. The DK page's area (181,035 km2) has no year.
